text: A function is a named, reusable block of code — write the logic once, run it as many times as you need with different inputs. Today covers declaring one, default parameters, and the one thing about return values that trips up every beginner.

A function takes parameters — placeholders it expects to receive — and the actual values passed in when it's called are the arguments. return sends a value back out. Everything after return inside the function never runs.

A default parameter value is used automatically whenever the caller doesn't pass that argument at all. This becomes genuinely useful once a function takes several optional settings, which is extremely common in real code.

A function declaration can be called earlier in the file than where it's written, because JavaScript hoists it. A function expression stored in a variable cannot — the variable doesn't exist yet at that point.

Here's the trap: a function with no return statement doesn't return nothing, it returns undefined, every time, silently. If a value shows up as undefined unexpectedly, check whether the function that produced it forgot to return.
Parameters and arguments, default values, declarations versus expressions, and the silent undefined return. Next up: arrays and objects — how you actually structure real data.
